ideas.title: See by clapping
ideas.goal: On a dark night a player claps and, for a moment, sees the island the way the sound found it: the surfaces the echo bounced off glow and fade. They find their hidden friends by clapping their way through the dark. Fun: a new sense, a real way to navigate, and every clap looks different depending on where you stand.
ideas.idea: The echo tracer I have (physics/echo.jl, 600k acoustic rays on Raycore's BVH in 0.13 s on the GPU) marks every hit with its arrival time and energy. The game splats those hits as short-lived glowing points on the real geometry, lit in arrival order, so a wave of light rolls out from the clap and comes back from the pond and the cottage wall. The sound you hear is the traced impulse response. Watching: dark island, a ring of light runs over the ground, trees light up from the side that faces the clap.
ideas.form: Engine physics (echo on the GPU, live) plus a night mini game (find the 4 hidden friends by clapping); a path traced film of a night clap.

ideas.title: Burning glass
ideas.goal: The player picks up a lens and focuses the sun onto dry leaves, a fuse or a friend's marshmallow until it smokes and catches. Fun: aim, find the focal distance, watch the bright spot shrink and the thing start to burn.
ideas.idea: The irradiance at the bright spot is traced through the real lens (a glass sphere cap, refraction, the sun's angular size), so the spot is only hot when it is sharp; the material heats by absorbed power and burns past its ignition temperature, spreading over a grid of dry grass. Watching: a white pinpoint on a leaf, a curl of smoke, a flame that creeps.
ideas.form: Physics (heat and combustion grid on the GPU, light from the tracer), a tool Lumi and the player hold, a film in path tracing where the caustic is real.

ideas.title: Skipping stones
ideas.goal: Throw a flat stone low at the sea and count the skips; spin, angle and speed decide. Fun: a skill people know from every beach, with a record to beat and rings left on the water.
ideas.idea: A rigid disc with spin meets the water surface: lift from the immersed area (the published stone skimming model, angle of attack near 20 degrees), drag, and gyroscopic stability; each touch launches a ripple ring on a wave height field that spreads and fades. Watching: a stone hopping farther and shorter, rings crossing each other.
ideas.form: Physics on the GPU (water height field, rigid disc), a mini game with a best count, a film.

ideas.title: Stones that ring
ideas.goal: Strike stones, planks and pots with a stick and hear the sound of their real shape; find stones in tune and lay a xylophone that the player plays. Fun: searching the island by ear and making music from found things.
ideas.idea: Modal sound synthesis: the FEM of each mesh (PrintSim's elastic solver) gives its vibration modes and frequencies; a strike excites them by where it hits, and they ring and decay by the material's damping. A big stone booms, a thin slate pings. Watching: Lumi tapping stones, the tones shown as rings on the stone.
ideas.form: Physics plus sound engine, a building mechanic (lay the lithophone), a film with sound.

ideas.title: Pump the swing
ideas.goal: A swing on the big tree: the player pumps it by leaning and tucking at the right moments, then lets go at the top and flies. Fun: a rhythm you feel, then a jump for distance.
ideas.idea: A rope pendulum with a body whose centre of mass shifts (parametric pumping, the real way children swing), rope from PrintSim rods and joints. Letting go is a ballistic launch into the meadow. Watching: the arc grows each swing, the rope slackens at the top.
ideas.form: Physics on the GPU, a play thing on the island, a film.

ideas.title: Paper planes
ideas.goal: Fold a sheet into a plane and throw it: how you folded it decides whether it glides, loops or dives. Fun: tinkering, a throw that is never the same twice.
ideas.idea: The paper sheet project continued: fold lines as hinges on the PrintSim sheet, the air drag with a pitching moment (todo #610), so a well-folded plane trims itself into a glide. Watching: a white plane over the meadow, stalling and recovering.
ideas.form: Physics (PrintSim sheet with air), a tool, the next step of project paper-letters, a film.

ideas.title: The sand castle and the tide
ideas.goal: Dig wet sand, pile and pat it into towers; the tide comes up and the waves eat it. Fun: build against time, wet sand stands steep, dry sand runs.
ideas.idea: Granular height field on the GPU with an angle of repose that depends on wetness; waves raise the water line and wet then wash the sand. Watching: towers slumping in slow avalanches.
ideas.form: Physics on the GPU, a beach play, a film.

ideas.title: Walk into the camera obscura
ideas.goal: The player walks into the dark hut and sees the island live, upside down on the wall, with the friends walking on the ceiling. Fun: a magic trick that is pure physics.
ideas.idea: Project camera-obscura next step: a deeper hut and a longer lens so the picture is sharp, traced live at low samples while the player stands inside.
ideas.form: Rendering, a place on the island, a film from inside.

ideas.title: Tug of war
ideas.goal: Lumi and a friend pull a rope; feet dig in and slide on grass, the one on the mud slips. Fun: a contest with a real winner.
ideas.idea: A rope of PrintSim rods, friction of the feet against the ground material, pulls from the creatures' strength. Watching: the rope taut, a friend skidding.
ideas.form: Physics, an interaction between creatures, a film.

ideas.title: Skating on the glass sea
ideas.goal: Skate on the frozen sea: blades carve marks that stay, turns spray frost. Fun: carving lines, drawing with your skates.
ideas.idea: Project glass-sea next step: ice friction along and across the blade, carved grooves in a frost texture that scatter light in the path tracer.
ideas.form: Physics and materials, a play, a film.
